topic: Sharp directed-fan-in frontier for numerical edge identification in confounded linear SEMs. Input: an acyclic mixed graph, rational feasible positive-definite covariance, and a queried directed coefficient; the fiber consists of all supported structural matrices whose induced noise covariance respects the bidirected graph. Prove a deterministic polynomial-bit algorithm at maximum directed indegree one using Möbius components plus singular 2-SAT clauses, returning a unique rational value, two unequal feasible witnesses, or a componentwise quadratic nonconstant-curve certificate. Prove promise universal-real completeness at indegree two via a fiber-bijective private-parent and occurrence-hub compiler with rational strictly diagonally dominant covariance. Preserve MIIVsem as the numerical-identification consumer and treat covariance-confidence-set inversion as secondary. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: indegree-one bi-affine equations were reduced to invertible Möbius components with quadratic-or-cofinite domains and singular equality disjunctions; indegree-two addition, multiplication, copying, repeated inputs, covariance-slot separation, and positive-definite witnesses passed bounded exact checks over 48 Möbius relations, 2,286 singular assignments, and two complete compilers. A global primitive element can have exponential degree, so certificates must remain componentwise quadratic. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: independently audit the arbitrary-input component normalization and 2-SAT equivalence, including poles and every singular degeneration, then verify a complete selector-circuit compiler. EARLY KILL TEST: compare the full component algorithm against real-algebraic elimination on bounded degenerate rational systems and eliminate every copy equation in a circuit using all primitives; any extra fiber branch kills the frontier. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_fanin_numedge_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For acyclic mixed graphs of maximum directed indegree one and feasible rational covariance matrices, can pointwise numerical identification of a queried directed coefficient be decided in deterministic polynomial bit complexity with constructive certificates for every singular degeneration?

source_refs.claim: Defines numerical edge identifiability at a feasible covariance and proves promise-universal-real hardness and membership for unrestricted acyclic mixed graphs, without a bounded-indegree frontier.
source_refs.author: Julian Dörfler, Benito van der Zander, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: Gives a randomized polynomial-time complete generic-identification algorithm when the directed component is a tree, classifying each coefficient as generically one-, two-, or infinitely identifiable through fractional affine square-root expressions.
source_refs.author: Aaryan Gupta, Markus Bläser

source_refs.claim: Shows that missing cycles of bidirected edges in tree-shaped linear SCMs yield explicit quadratic systems with one or two candidate solutions, but treats generic symbolic identification rather than all numerical fibers.
source_refs.author: Benito van der Zander, Marcel Wienöbst, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

open_problems.why_unsolved: The complete tree-shaped algorithms exploit generic nonvanishing and return symbolic one/two/infinite classifications, whereas numerical identification must remain correct on the exceptional covariance locus where denominators vanish, Möbius transformations acquire poles, and quadratic equations collapse to linear, tautological, or inconsistent relations. The general real-algebraic decision procedure handles those points only in PSPACE and supplies no low-degree constructive certificate. The retrieved literature contains tree-specific generic algorithms and unrestricted numerical hardness, but no complete deterministic bit-polynomial treatment of arbitrary indegree-one forests coupled through unrestricted bidirected components.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a deterministic polynomial-bit fiber algorithm that returns either the unique rational queried coefficient, two unequal feasible parameter witnesses, or a componentwise degree-at-most-two rational/algebraic parametrization certifying a nonconstant feasible curve, with a proof covering poles and every singular equation degeneration.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing cleanly separates graph-level generic identification from covariance-specific numerical identification and makes computational complexity the organizing question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Linear SEM coefficients are causal quantities hidden by correlated errors -> generic graphical criteria do not decide exceptional numerical fibers -> unrestricted numerical identification is universal-real hard -> isolate maximum directed indegree one as the candidate exact tractable boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert missing-bidirected-cycle constraints into coupled quadratic equations and combine cycles to eliminate the spurious root; the proof explicitly tracks the one-versus-two-solution alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its quadratic fiber structure is the nearest established analogue of the componentwise quadratic certificates required for arbitrary indegree-one mixed graphs.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent tree-model coefficient solutions by fractional affine square-root terms and prove the generic one/two/infinite trichotomy using polynomial identity testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a complete low-degree symbolic representation on the tree subclass; the new work must replace generic identity tests by exact pointwise normalization across singular strata.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate recursively defined rational half-trek moment equations to obtain an influence function, asymptotic variance, and Wald inference while propagating uncertainty from earlier identification stages.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On regular singleton strata, an indegree-one exact recovery map is likewise assembled from local rational equations, so the recursive delta-method argument is the natural estimation-and-inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Does promise numerical identification of a queried directed coefficient remain universal-real complete when the acyclic mixed graph has maximum directed indegree two and the rational feasible covariance is required to be strictly diagonally dominant?

source_refs.claim: Proves universal-real hardness for numerical edge identifiability by programming quadratic equations into covariance constraints; its construction stores arbitrarily many variables as coefficients entering a common node and therefore does not establish bounded-indegree hardness.
source_refs.author: Julian Dörfler, Benito van der Zander, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: Places generic identification in randomized polynomial time for the tree-shaped subclass, sharpening the need to locate which small departure from directed fan-in one permits full real-algebraic hardness.
source_refs.author: Aaryan Gupta, Markus Bläser

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known hardness reduction obtains freely programmable bilinear covariance equations by routing all source variables into a storage node, so its maximum directed indegree grows with the encoded real-algebraic instance. Replacing that hub by fan-in-two addition, multiplication, copying, and occurrence-routing gadgets is not merely a circuit-size exercise: each gadget must preserve the entire feasible fiber, prevent extra real branches, keep covariance entries from unintentionally coupling distinct constraints, and retain positive definiteness with polynomial-bit rational data. Focused searches recovered no bounded-indegree numerical-identifiability lower bound, while the closest low-indegree results concern generic tree identification.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a polynomial-time many-one reduction from a planted-solution quadratic feasibility problem to feasible rational instances of numerical edge identification with directed indegree at most two, together with a fiber bijection and a rational strict-diagonal-dominance proof, matched by the existing promise-universal-real upper bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the exact complexity vocabulary, planted-solution promise formulation, and numerical edge-fiber target that the bounded-fan-in refinement must preserve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Numerical identification is a covariance-specific fiber question -> unrestricted fibers can encode arbitrary quadratic real systems -> the published reduction uses an unbounded storage hub -> determine whether fan-in two already supports a fiber-faithful universal-real compiler.

method_exemplars.technique: Plant a distinguished solution in a QUAD instance, program affine and multiplication constraints through missing-bidirected-edge covariance equations, and project the fiber onto the distinguished coefficient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result keeps the same source problem and edge-fiber equivalence; only the unbounded storage and equation-programming layout must be replaced by bounded-fan-in, occurrence-separated gadgets.

open_problems.open_problem: Can MIIV and latent-to-observed SEM workflows be equipped with an exact pointwise numerical-identification audit that detects covariance-specific rank failures and returns either the unique queried loading or path coefficient or explicit observationally equivalent feasible witnesses?

source_refs.claim: Presents MIIV-2SLS as an equation-by-equation SEM estimator, emphasizes weak instruments and structural misspecification, and identifies extensions and open questions for MIIV practice.
source_refs.author: Kenneth A. Bollen

source_refs.claim: Proves equivalence between the graphical latent-to-observed transformation with instrumental sets and the MIIV approach, while supplying non-iterative generic parameter-identification strategies.
source_refs.author: Ankur Ankan, Inge Wortel, Kenneth Bollen, Johannes Textor

source_refs.claim: Formalizes numerical edge identifiability as uniqueness of a coefficient over the complete feasible fiber at the supplied covariance, rather than generic validity of an identifying formula.
source_refs.author: Julian Dörfler, Benito van der Zander, Markus Bläser, Maciej Liśkiewicz

open_problems.why_unsolved: MIIV selection and the L2O equivalence are graph- and model-level results whose estimators require nonzero first-stage covariance or full-rank moment matrices at the realized law. At singular feasible covariances, failure of a chosen MIIV denominator does not itself establish nonidentification because another algebraic route may still identify the coefficient; conversely, generic identification does not rule out multiple values on that exceptional fiber. Existing MIIV software reports weak-instrument diagnostics and overidentification tests, but the retrieved methodological papers do not provide a complete exact fiber audit or constructive alternative SEM witnesses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a sound-and-complete algorithmic characterization linking the L2O-transformed covariance fiber to the original latent-variable coefficient, returning its unique exact value or two feasible observationally equivalent latent-SEM parameterizations, plus regularity conditions under which the audited coefficient admits MIIV-GMM limit theory.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames MIIV as a practical equation-by-equation alternative to full-information SEM estimation and foregrounds weak instruments, diagnostics, and model misspecification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Full-information SEM estimators can obscure local misspecification -> MIIV supplies transparent equation-level instruments and tests -> realized instruments may be weak or exactly singular -> add a complete pointwise identification audit before reporting a structural coefficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the graphical latent-to-observed transformation and prove its equivalence to algebraic MIIV selection via instrumental-set criteria.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The audit must transfer coefficient uniqueness and alternative witnesses between the original latent model and the observed mixed-graph representation, exactly the correspondence established generically by L2O.

method_exemplars.technique: Express equality to a fixed covariance as polynomial fiber equations and test whether two feasible parameterizations can disagree on the queried edge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the direct pointwise replacement for concluding identification from the existence of a generic MIIV formula.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct equation-specific MIIV-GMM estimators and derive robust sandwich inference under latent-variable SEM moment restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once the exact audit establishes a regular singleton coefficient, MIIV-GMM is the natural consumer-facing estimator and limit-law framework.

open_problems.open_problem: For numerically identified direct effects in fan-in-one confounded linear SEMs, can one characterize the exact local conditioning of the recovery map and obtain inference that remains valid as the covariance approaches a pole, rank collapse, or fiber-bifurcation locus?

source_refs.claim: Shows that robust identifiability is strictly stronger than generic identifiability and proves high-probability sufficient conditions for bow-free models, while describing robust identification as poorly understood.
source_refs.author: Karthik A. Sankararaman, Anand Louis, Navin Goyal

source_refs.claim: Derives influence functions and asymptotic normality for regular HTC rational estimators under an invertible identification matrix, leaving singular and nearly singular numerical fibers outside its regular theory.
source_refs.author: Leopold Mareis, Nils Sturma, Mathias Drton

source_refs.claim: Characterizes valid conditional instrumental sets and compares their asymptotic variances, but conditions validity and inference on nonzero instrument relevance rather than covering approach to exact rank failure.
source_refs.author: Leonard Henckel, Martin Buttenschön, Marloes H. Maathuis

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular influence-function and 2SLS variance formulas invert a local moment matrix, while exact numerical identification can survive through alternative equations even when a particular determinant or MIIV denominator vanishes. Conversely, a singleton fiber at a tangency or repeated quadratic root can be point identified but nonregular, so a standard delta-method interval is not justified. Existing robust-identifiability results give sufficient norm bounds for bow-free recovery and high-probability statements under random parameters; they do not identify the exact singular strata of arbitrary fan-in-one confounded fibers or provide coverage across changes in fiber cardinality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A resolution would be a stratum-specific condition-number formula and limit theory for the queried direct effect, including a regular asymptotic-normal regime and a uniformly valid confidence-set or impossibility characterization for local sequences approaching poles, discriminant zero, or nonconstant-fiber strata.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why generic recoverability is insufficient for data analysis and organizes the problem around perturbations of the observational covariance.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Generic identification holds away from a null set -> small covariance errors can nevertheless cause large parameter errors -> robust identification needs quantitative conditioning -> classify regular and nonregular behavior at the exact fan-in-one numerical frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Define a covariance-to-parameter condition number and propagate spectral-norm perturbations through sequential linear recovery equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result needs the same perturbation calculus, but localized to Möbius and quadratic component maps and sharpened to blow-up rates at their singular loci.

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate identification equations, recursively correct for previously estimated coefficients, and express the influence-function variance through observable fourth moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the regular-stratum inference template; the unresolved step is replacing global matrix invertibility by a complete stratum analysis and treating local sequences where derivatives diverge or cease to exist.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive graphical validity and asymptotic-variance comparisons for conditional-instrumental-set 2SLS estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a consumer-facing variance benchmark for regular instrument strata against which confidence procedures near exact rank failure can be compared.

literature_map:
Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz (NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2407.12528) sharply separate generic from covariance-specific numerical identification and prove promise-universal-real completeness for unrestricted numerical edge identification.
Their hardness construction programs quadratic equations into missing-bidirected-edge constraints, but its variable-storage node has unbounded directed fan-in; no retrieved paper establishes bounded-fan-in numerical hardness.
Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant (Annals of Statistics 2011, arXiv:1003.1146) characterize graph-wide global identifiability, a stronger property than uniqueness at one supplied covariance.
Foygel, Draisma, and Drton (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1107.5552) give the polynomial-time half-trek sufficient criterion for generic rational identification and document many HTC-inconclusive graphs.
Drton and Weihs (Scandinavian Journal of Statistics 2017, arXiv:1504.02992) enlarge generic coverage through ancestral decomposition, still without resolving exceptional numerical fibers.
Weihs et al. (Journal of Causal Inference 2018, arXiv:1702.03884) recover individual edges as quotients of covariance subdeterminants, making poles and rank collapses explicit but generic.
Chen, Kumor, and Bareinboim (ICML 2017) and Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim (ICML 2020) develop auxiliary-variable and auxiliary-cutset identification, powerful polynomial-time sufficient methods rather than complete numerical tests.
Van der Zander et al. (AISTATS 2022, arXiv:2203.01852) expose quadratic one/two-solution structure from missing bidirected cycles in directed trees.
Gupta and Bläser (AAAI 2024, arXiv:2311.14058) give a complete randomized polynomial-time generic classification for tree-shaped SCMs using fractional affine square-root terms.
Briefs and Bläser (NeurIPS 2025) accelerate generic tree identification to near-cubic time, underscoring that the active low-fan-in literature remains generic rather than pointwise numerical.
Ankan, Wortel, Bollen, and Textor (AISTATS 2023) prove an L2O-plus-instrumental-set equivalence to MIIV, linking graphical identification to the MIIVsem consumer.
Bollen (Multivariate Behavioral Research 2019) and Bollen, Kolenikov, and Bauldry (Psychometrika 2014) provide MIIV-2SLS/GMM estimation and diagnostics, but not exact exceptional-fiber certificates.
Sankararaman, Louis, and Goyal (UAI 2020; UAI 2022, arXiv:1905.06836 and arXiv:2007.06869) show robust identification is stronger than generic identification and give condition-number bounds for bow-free models.
Mareis, Sturma, and Drton (2026, arXiv:2606.26931) derive regular semiparametric inference for HTC estimators; singular and fiber-bifurcation regimes remain outside that theory.
The central tension is therefore live: low-fan-in/tree structure yields low-degree generic algebra, while complete numerical edge identification is known universal-real hard only through reductions that do not preserve bounded directed fan-in.
